raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### Purpose
Fixes #54425.
Addresses the remaining seeded native sampling warmup gap from #54425 while aligning with #62129 to prevent pipeline parallel deadlocks.

### Problem
1. **Unwarmed Fallback Kernels (#54425)**: Under V1 with fused sampling enabled (`sampler.use_flashinfer` or `sampler.use_xpu_sampler`), `warmup_kernels()` only exercises default unseeded `SamplingParams`. Requests with an explicit `seed` bypass fused sampling (`fused_sampler_eligible` is False) and fall back to PyTorch-native top-k/top-p and Gumbel sampling. This causes JIT compilation and memory allocation latency spikes on the first seeded request.
2. **PP Rank Asymmetry (#62129)**: Under pipeline parallelism (`PP > 1`), `self.sampler` is initialized strictly on the last PP rank. Non-last ranks have `self.sampler = None`. Gating the warmup pass purely on rank-local `sampler is not None` causes non-last ranks to skip the pass while the last rank attempts to receive activations, deadlocking the engine on startup.

### Solution
- **Symmetric Warmup Pass**: Add a dedicated `seeded=True` warmup pass in `warmup_kernels()` that gates on `flashinfer_sampler_supported()` / `xpu_sampler_supported()` when `sampler is None`. All PP ranks execute the same forward passes in lockstep, eliminating startup deadlocks. Unfused configurations skip this pass with zero overhead.
- **Tests**:
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_mixed_warmup_gate.py`: Parameterized across `is_last_pp_rank: [False, True]` and `fused_backend: ["flashinfer", "xpu", None]` to assert all PP ranks stay in sync.
  - `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_sampler_flags.py`: Verifies `any_explicit_seed()` evaluates correctly on GPU and resets on slot reuse.

### Verification
- Replicated pipeline parallel execution and verified the pre-fix deadlock and post-fix lockstep completion.
- Tested on NVIDIA A100: confirmed seeded requests fall back to native kernels cleanly without latency spikes.
- Pre-commit checks pass cleanly (`ruff check`, `ruff format`).

### AI Usage Disclaimer
The architecture, diagnostic analysis, root-cause investigation, and design choices for this fix are entirely my own. AI tooling was utilized solely as an assistant for refining test case parameterization and code review critique.

🚀

Tested on Intel XPU. **It fixes it: 3 JIT compilations → 0, and the first-request penalty
drops from +94% to +15%.**

**Setup**: 1× Intel Arc Pro B70, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MXFP4, spec decode `qwen3_5_mtp`
(`num_speculative_tokens=2`), `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, `kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
Patch applied as a diff onto `cacc429f6` (all three files applied cleanly). Requests are
`temperature=0` — the path #54455 was about. **No warmup workaround of my own in either arm**,
otherwise the control would not show the effect.

```
                   1st req    reqs 2-4    penalty        JIT warnings
control (no PR)     1.127 s     0.581 s   +93.7% (+545 ms)     3
this PR             0.664 s     0.581 s   +14.5%  (+84 ms)     0
```

The three that disappear are exactly the ones from the report:
`_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`, `_rejection_kernel`, `_resample_kernel`.

Steady state is identical (0.581 s in both), so no regression on this box.

**One honest note**: the remaining +84 ms is *not* JIT — `jit_monitor` reports zero. So there
is some other first-request cost left over that this PR is not responsible for and that I have
not chased. Worth knowing if someone measures the same thing and wonders why it is not 0%.
Thanks a lot @TSUMUGI-XE for testing this on Intel XPU!

_🚀 Performance & Scalability_ | _🟠 Major_ | _🏗️ Heavy lift_

**Warm all configurations when fewer than three requests fit.**

`num_reqs` can be 1 or 2 because scheduler and KV-cache limits are applied before this list is consumed. Cycling the list then creates only the first one or two configurations, and the greedy decode steps are skipped unless `num_reqs >= 3`. A one-request warmup never exercises seeded or greedy sampling. A two-request warmup never exercises greedy sampling. Run separate warmup passes for configurations that do not fit in one batch.

Tested on Intel XPU. **It fixes it: 3 JIT compilations → 0, and the first-request penalty
drops from +94% to +15%.**

**Setup**: 1× Intel Arc Pro B70, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MXFP4, spec decode `qwen3_5_mtp`
(`num_speculative_tokens=2`), `cudagraph_mode=FULL_DECODE_ONLY`, `kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
Patch applied as a diff onto `cacc429f6` (all three files applied cleanly). Requests are
`temperature=0` — the path #54455 was about. **No warmup workaround of my own in either arm**,
otherwise the control would not show the effect.

```
                   1st req    reqs 2-4    penalty        JIT warnings
control (no PR)     1.127 s     0.581 s   +93.7% (+545 ms)     3
this PR             0.664 s     0.581 s   +14.5%  (+84 ms)     0
```

The three that disappear are exactly the ones from the report:
`_compute_local_logits_stats_kernel`, `_rejection_kernel`, `_resample_kernel`.

Steady state is identical (0.581 s in both), so no regression on this box.

**One honest note**: the remaining +84 ms is *not* JIT — `jit_monitor` reports zero. So there
is some other first-request cost left over that this PR is not responsible for and that I have
not chased. Worth knowing if someone measures the same thing and wonders why it is not 0%.
Thanks a lot @TSUMUGI-XE for testing this on Intel XPU!
